findings.title: exportXml mutates the live retained document outside the atomic commit and lock
findings.why_it_matters: The public export path passes the active document directly to a serializer that first rewrites diagram-index state and later replaces sourceXml/sourceIds. Unlike mutations, it neither clones the document nor takes the per-process lock. A serialization failure can therefore leave the in-memory process partially reconciled even though export rejected, and an export concurrent with a save/mutation can observe or modify the same state outside the transaction that guarantees disk/memory consistency.
findings.suggested_fix: Make export a pure serialization of a clone, or route it through the same per-process lock and commit-style copy-on-write boundary while keeping export non-persistent. Move synchronization side effects behind that boundary so errors cannot alter the live context.
evidence: exportXml calls serializer.serialize(context.document, formatted) directly (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:320-323), whereas commitMutation clones and locks before serialization (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:496-534).

serialize immediately invokes synchronizeDiagramInterchange, which adds/removes document.diagram shapes and edges in place (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:150-206 and 212-215), before retained parsing or toXML can fail.

Both serializer paths assign document.sourceXml and expand sourceIds in place after serialization (src/core/BpmnDocument.ts:396-397 and 515-516); export takes no lock while commitMutation's lock is only entered by mutation/save methods.

residual_risks: The write path itself has strong coverage for temporary-file cleanup, failed writes, and same-process concurrent mutations, but it cannot make uncoordinated direct ProcessContext/document mutations safe.

Parsing and retained reconciliation run in-process without cancellation or a time budget; byte, element, flow, and DI limits bound input size but not CPU cost for pathological XML within those limits.
testing_gaps: Inject a retained-serializer failure through exportXml and assert the live document's sourceXml, sourceIds, shapes, edges, and current XML remain unchanged.
Exercise exportXml concurrently with an autosaved retained-document mutation and assert deterministic XML plus no disk/context divergence.

The focused import-roundtrip test covers malformed-import atomicity, while persistence tests cover serializer/write rollback and mutation locking; neither covers export failure or export/mutation interleaving.
